ui.subtitle: For the Creality Ender-3 V3 (220 × 220 × 250 mm build volume). Everything is computed on this computer, no photo goes online.
ui.tip_base: Cuts the bottom of the model flat so it stands up on the bed. 3% suits a bust; 0 keeps the whole model.
ui.tip_color: The first two files need a printer with several spools; the Ender-3 V3 on its own has only one. Painted 3MF: each face gets a filament number, not a color; in OrcaSlicer, first set up as many filaments as the palette has, in this order and with these colors, then open it. File > Import adds the missing filaments, but their colors need fixing. Colored OBJ: OrcaSlicer (2.1 or newer) opens a window that adds these colors as filaments, give or take a few units; keep the .mtl next to the .obj. Textured OBJ: all the photo colors, for a color printing service (Sculpteo, i.materialise…). The colors come from the photos, shadows included.
ui.tip_color_files: Computed on top of the STL when the photos provide colors. Only the checked files are computed; the texture of the textured OBJ adds a few seconds to a minute.
ui.tip_export_box: Real size in meters, Y up, base centered on the origin. 3D software: quads, 4096 textures, .blend, FBX and OBJ files; to animate a character, a manual retopology is still useful. Games: triangles in 3 levels of detail (100, 50 and 25%), 2048 textures, FBX and GLB. Web: a GLB of a few MB, plus a Draco-compressed version when this Blender produces one. Textures: the photo colors, shadows included, and a normal map for fine relief.
ui.tip_exports: The model cleaned up for uses other than printing, at its real size in meters, on top of the print files. One zip per checked profile. Each one makes the computation longer: about 15 s for Web or Games and over a minute for 3D software on a simple model, more on a detailed scan.
ui.tip_faces: Number of facets in the LowPoly style. Fewer facets give a more angular model.
ui.tip_filaments: Number of colors in the painted 3MF and the colored OBJ, one per spool on your printer. The photo colors are grouped into that many shades, or fewer if the object has fewer.
ui.tip_files: STL: the standard 3D printing file, accepted by every slicer. .blend: Blender file, to touch up the model. The files are copied to Downloads.
ui.tip_height: Height of the model once printed. The Ender-3 V3 prints up to 245 mm tall.
ui.tip_level: LowPoly: large facets, the fastest. Medium: smoother. Detailed: the most faithful to the photos, the slowest. The first reconstruction takes one to several minutes depending on the photos and the computer; the other levels are then generated in one click.
ui.tip_levels: Each level starts from the same photos. Check the shape in LowPoly, then generate more detail if you like it. Click a level already computed to show it.
ui.tip_mode: Automatic chooses for you: with 20 photos or more, the model is reconstructed from all the photos; with fewer, the AI estimates the shape from a single photo.
ui.tip_nozzle: Nozzle diameter. The Ender-3 V3 ships with 0.4 mm. Walls thinner than twice the nozzle are flagged.
ui.tip_parts: By default, only the largest piece is kept and the debris is removed. Check this if your model has several intended parts.
ui.tip_rotate: Is the model lying down or crooked? Turn it a quarter turn: the preview turns right away, then click "Recompute with this orientation" to apply it.
ui.tip_smooth: Softens small bumps and scan grain. Strong smoothing also rounds off fine details (nose, ears, locks of hair); wall thickness is checked again on every computation. You can also change it afterwards, in "Adjust this model".
ui.tip_smooth_adjust: Softens small bumps and scan grain. Strong smoothing also rounds off fine details (nose, ears, locks of hair); wall thickness is checked again when recomputing.
